title: Research to Understand Number of Children Singaporean Women Would Like to Have
what_it_is: Research to Understand Number of Children Singaporean Women Would Like to Have

sections.label: Marriage and Parenthood Survey findings
sections.summary: The 2021 survey of about 6,000 respondents found women want at least two children on average, but married women had fewer, citing cost, stress and work-family demands.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: According to the 2021 Marriage and Parenthood Survey of about 6,000 respondents, Singaporean women want to have at least two children on average.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: However, in practice, married female respondents had less than two children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Common reasons cited for not having more children include concerns over the financial cost and stress of raising children, and difficulties in managing work and family demands.

sections.label: Survey results publicly available
sections.summary: The survey results are publicly available.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The survey results are, in fact, publicly available.

sections.label: Survey dates and respondents
sections.summary: The survey ran February to June 2021 with 2,848 single and 3,017 married Singapore residents aged 21 to 45, and its highlights do not indicate housing prices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The survey was conducted from February to June 2021, with respondents comprising 2,848 single – that means, never married – and 3,017 married Singapore residents, aged 21 to 45 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The highlights of the survey do not indicate housing prices, as Mr Perera mentioned.

sections.label: Factors affecting parenthood decisions
sections.summary: The survey showed key considerations in parenthood decisions included managing child-raising costs and work and family commitments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In terms of the factors that affected having children, the survey showed that in making parenthood decisions, key considerations included the ability to manage the costs of child-raising, as well as to manage work and family commitments.

sections.label: Financial support for parents
sections.summary: The measures are directed towards financial support for parents, including the Baby Bonus cash gift increase, CDA top-up and enhanced CDA co-matching.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The measures are directed towards financial support for parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, the increase in the Baby Bonus cash gift, the Child Development Account (CDA) top-up, the enhancement of the CDA co-matching.
